images.title: Divide coefficients, subtract exponents
images.purpose: Shows ants per human: 2 × 10 to the power 16 divided by 8 × 10 to the power 9 gives 2.5 × 10 to the power 6.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. A fraction on the left, two small working boxes in the middle and the answer on the right, in one row.
images.exact_structure: Left: a fraction with '2 × 10¹⁶' above the bar and '8 × 10⁹' below it; the coefficients 2 and 8 in teal (#0072B2), the powers of 10 in amber (#E69F00). An arrow right to two stacked small boxes: a teal (#0072B2) outlined box with '2 ÷ 8 = 0.25' and an amber (#E69F00) outlined box with '16 − 9 = 7'. An arrow right to '0.25 × 10⁷', then an arrow to '2.5 × 10⁶' in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. Exactly 1 fraction, 2 working boxes, 3 arrows, 1 answer box.

images.takeaway: To divide in scientific notation, divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents, then tidy the coefficient.
images.description: Shows ants per human: 2 × 10 to the power 16 divided by 8 × 10 to the power 9 gives 2.5 × 10 to the power 6.
images.context: 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25 and 16 − 9 = 7, so 0.25 × 10 to the power 7, which is 2.5 × 10 to the power 6 ants per human.
images.teaching_notes: Multiplying works the same way with the coefficients multiplied and the exponents added.

image_decisions.why: Splitting the work into coefficients and exponents is the one method this concept teaches.
